doc.title: Buddy Burns and Frank Pasley Interview, 1968-09-23

title: Udell Wilson and Willie Jackson at the Lyric Theater
summary: He recalls pianist Udell Wilson playing a cabaret with singer Willie Jackson near the Lyric Theater, and Charlie Love and other trumpeters.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: wasn't he? He came from Kansas City. He came from Kansas City, yeah, I was told so. Was he older than
you? Oh, yeah. And somebody told me he was bald-headed. That's true? No, not at that time when I knew him, no.
When did you first meet him? About 1919. 1919. At this time, do you know when he came into New Orleans

from Kansas City? I don't know when he came, but he was already there. He was already there, because it was a theater called the Lyric Theater, and he played right across the street at that cabaret upstairs there, him and Willie Jackson. At the Lyric Theater, or across? No, at the Lyric Theater,
that's right there on there. Yeah, and he played with Willie Jackson, and did they have anybody else?

No, just the two. Not Charlie Love on trumpet? No. No. Only boys I know named Love played trumpet. They were from Texas. Charlie Love? Yeah, he was from Texas. Yeah. And it was one of the Loves played on the boat there with Faith, with Faith Marvel. A trumpet player? Yeah, a trumpet player. He was from either Houston or Dallas, or one.

Yeah. Yeah. Charlie Love. Yeah. He was a good trumpet player. Yeah. He could play ractime and all those tricky stuff. Yeah. And Willie Jackson used to sing. What did he sing, Willie Jackson? Blues. And? Mostly blues, popular songs, and things like that. And this was in 19... 1918, 1919. Oh yeah, that early. Yeah, way back there. Yeah. Willie Jackson made some records in New Orleans. Yeah. I don't know which one it was, but he made them. Yeah. Yeah. I was there when Bessie Smith come there the first time. At the Lyric? No. She came. She went to...
